__: Shared cases for the schema-shadowing rule (docs/DESIGN.md §3.1), read by BOTH implementations' test suites: crates/pve-meta-core (registry::governing) and ui-extjs/testing/smoke.js (PVE.meta.Utils.governing). Add a case here, never to one suite -- the same reasoning as testdata/covers-cases.json, and the same failure it prevents.
__note_on_shape: Each case gives the declared prefixes in ARBITRARY order, the guest's tags, a path, and which prefix governs it (null for none). The two sides factor this differently -- Rust's `governing` filters by selector itself, while the editor filters first (`applicablePrefixes`) and then asks -- and both must sort most-specific-first before asking (`load_prefixes` / `bySpecificity`). Handing over an unsorted list with selectors makes each side run its whole chain, which is the composite rule a user actually meets, rather than the one function each happens to have factored out.

cases.why: most specific wins; the parent's own `properties.docker` is shadowed, never merged
a sibling of the nested prefix falls back to the parent
the prefix governs its own key
no prefix covers it, so nothing describes its shape
the document root is above every prefix, not under one
a longer name is not a child -- the separator is what makes one
the more specific prefix's selector missed, so a prefix that does reach this guest governs -- shadowing is decided among the prefixes that apply, not among all of them
and once its selector matches, the more specific one takes over
an untagged guest is not reached by a tag selector at all
an all-guests prefix is the fallback when the more specific one's tag is absent
... and adding the tag hands that subtree to the more specific one

shape uses plain containment, NOT the permission rule `covers`: a scope on `a` may write the note about `a`, but a prefix `a` does not describe the shape of a prefix named `a__`. Two predicates, two jobs (testdata/covers-cases.json has the other one)
and with no `a__` declared, nothing describes it -- `covers` would have said `a` did
a comment key *inside* the subtree is part of it, on both rules
three levels, handed over out of order: each side must sort by specificity before it asks
... and the answer changes with the path, not with the input order
